disclaimer: Intervention effects are untested pilots, not measured savings.

rows.trigger: Creation-to-final-notification > observed P90 (23.927 min); descriptive case-review cutoff
rows.action: Instrument first dispatch and reassignment; review high-delay orders before testing an escalation workflow.
rows.monitoring_kpi: P90 creation-to-final-notification, late >5min, completion, recorded cost per reviewed order
rows.trade_off: Premature escalation and manual review add effort; validate a small pilot.
rows.confidence: Supported descriptive cohort; intervention effect untested

rows.trigger: Final-rider pickup waiting > observed P90 (9.816 min)
rows.action: Review merchant readiness and rider arrival coordination in supported merchant cohorts.
rows.monitoring_kpi: Pickup wait P90, service P90, late >5min, completion
rows.trade_off: Later rider arrival can reduce waiting but delay delivery if readiness is misestimated.
rows.confidence: Supported descriptive cohort; intervention effect untested

rows.trigger: At least four recorded pre events; a review cohort, not a calibrated optimum
rows.action: Pilot exception review and capture why repeated assignments fail.
rows.monitoring_kpi: Time to final notification, pre-event count, completion, late >5min, recorded cost
rows.trade_off: Intervention can increase incentives or manual work; measure the trade-off.
rows.confidence: Supported descriptive cohort; intervention effect untested

findings.title: The main measured deterioration occurs before the final rider notification
findings.observation: Creation to final notification averages 10.58 minutes. It contributes 6.05 minutes, or 51.0%, of the late-versus-on-time duration difference. Pickup waiting contributes 24.0%.
findings.action: Capture first-dispatch, offer, acceptance and reassignment timestamps. Review long initial intervals before choosing a dispatch intervention.
findings.limitation: A time decomposition identifies where time accrues; it does not identify a causal dispatch mechanism.

findings.title: A small repeated-pre-event cohort concentrates operational problems
findings.observation: 10,472 orders with at least four pre events represent 3.1% of orders with known pre counts and 36.6% of recorded pre events. Their completed orders average 45.88 minutes; 67.1% exceed the promise by more than five minutes.
findings.action: Pilot review after four recorded pre events, checking unresolved assignment and merchant readiness. Track time to final notification, completion, late >5 minutes and recorded cost per reviewed order.
findings.confidence: Strong concentration evidence; pilot effect untested
findings.limitation: Four is a diagnostic grouping, not an optimized trigger. Final-state counters do not reveal attempt order, offer compensation or rejecting rider identity.

findings.title: Longer recorded delivery distances identify a high-pre-event population
findings.observation: Orders with recorded dropoff distance above 3 km have 47.9% pre-event incidence, versus 17.3% at 1 km or less. The difference is 30.59 percentage points, with a 95% date-bootstrap interval of 29.49–31.61 points.
findings.action: Review long-distance offers by service vertical and clock hour, logging offered compensation, assignment sequence and time to final notification. Test an assignment-policy change with pre incidence, service tails and recorded cost guardrails.
findings.confidence: Strong descriptive association; pricing mechanism untested
findings.limitation: Distance units follow the project's metre interpretation; route and offer-level evidence is incomplete. This supports targeted investigation rather than a causal price recommendation.
